item.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
item.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

item.title: People who opposed Tinubu now work with him — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question for those who want to vote,” Fashola said. He asked why many of those who worked with Tinubu during his time as Lagos governor had remained with him, while political associates of other candidates had moved on. “Where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team, and you don’t just get up and jump away when there is crisis in the fold,” he said. He contrasted Tinubu’s political experience with that of other candidates, saying the president remained in the APC despite internal crises, while others left the parties through which they rose to prominence. “There was crisis in the APC. He didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence,” Fashola said. The former governor further argued that Tinubu had expanded his political alliances by bringing former opponents into his fold, including those who once strongly opposed him. “All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing. All of them are now working with him. Not just those who worked with him before; those who oppose him are now working with him,” he said. item.title: ‘What a joke’ – Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany calls out NFL’s bias against Chiefs after Bills loss
item.description: Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/NWSL via Getty Images Brittany Mahomes didn’t mince her words about the NFL’s officiating after the Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Day defeat. The Buffalo Bills walked away with a 13-10 win over Super Bowl favourites Kansas City Chiefs in a closely contested 2026 Thanksgiving Day clash. However, the Bills’ win came with a plethora of criticism for the NFL from the Chiefs fanbase, including star QB Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany. The 31-year-old expressed her frustration over the highly debated overturned call in the fourth quarter. Brittany Mahomes lashes out at NFL officiating The moment that caught Brittany’s attention was an overturned catch by Rashee Rice in the fourth quarter of the Thanksgiving Day defeat. Mahomes called out the controversial decision in one of her Instagram stories, highlighted by NFL insider Ari Meirov on X . “HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE. Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that, I guess? I don’t wanna hear s___ anymore from anyone,” Mahomes wrote. Considering the overturned play ultimately turned into a game-winning field goal at the buzzer for the Bills, Mahomes’ frustration is understandable. In fact, most NFL fans on social media resonated with the former soccer star’s sentiments and felt that the Chiefs were robbed of a clear catch. Following the three-point defeat, the Chiefs have now fallen to an 8-3 record, while the Bills are now 10-1 and look the outright favourites to win the Super Bowl this season. item.title: Poole's 100-game Pompey adventure
item.description: [Shutterstock] [BBC] In the summer of 2023 free agent Regan Poole turned down a higher salary elsewhere in League One to sign for Portsmouth. He did so believing the move to the south coast presented him with the best opportunity of reaching the Championship and furthering his career. Exactly 100 appearances later, he's been proved correct. Just like Poole's entire career trajectory, his time at Portsmouth has had plenty of ups and downs. After an excellent start and an international debut for Wales, he tore his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during an FA Cup defeat at Chesterfield. When he returned, Pompey were struggling to adjust to life in the Championship and the transition wasn't straightforward for Poole. Not helped by having to play many games in quick succession following a serious injury. Poole and Pompey improved and maintained their Championship status. Portsmouth spent, by their standards, significant fees on centre-backs Hayden Matthews and Josh Knight. Neither have looked like dislodging Poole. Even this season Poole struggled at the start, affected by injury and then below Benji Arthur and Conor Shaughnessy in the pecking order. He's fought his way back into the side and now looks every inch the Championship centre-back he was hoping to become. Portsmouth fans always appreciate committed players. Fratton Park is a ground where big tackles get a louder cheers than great pieces of skills. Poole puts his body on the line the way the home fans crave to see. He wears his heart on his sleeve, celebrating great tackles and blocks. He's absolutely buzzing after wins and often has a face of thunder after defeats (although he will front up to the media). Likely in a similar way to fans leaving the ground. Supporters also love to go on a journey with a player. Poole has grown and improved with the team in the nearly three and half years he's been here. His journey through football has been fascinating , making his Newport County debut at just 16 before moving to Manchester United and then fighting his way back up through the EFL. He's now going into the final year of his contract and has made it clear he would love to sign a new one . The club retain an option year in his deal so it seems very unlikely he'll be departing anytime soon. I highly doubt John Mousinho and Richard Hughes mentioned the Premier League when trying to sell the club to Poole. It would still require something miraculous for Pompey to reach the top flight imminently. But the fact I'm even mentioning it highlights what an adventure the first 100 Pompey matches have been for Regan Poole. item.title: Cruz Azul crush Leon and look set to go thru to the Semifinals
item.description: Cruz Azul's Argentine forward #20 Jose Paradela celebrate a goal during the Liga MX Apertura Liguilla quarter-final first-leg football match between Leon and Cruz Azul at the Leon Stadium in Leon, Mexico on November 26, 2026. (Photo by Mario ARMAS / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Cruz Azul demolished Leon by a 4-0 score in the first leg of the Quarterfinals series and looks to have settled the Quarterfinal series. Leon must not only win by 5 goals on Sunday but they must do so as the away team against the current Liga MX title. Cruz Azul was overly superior to a Leon team that looked rattled from the start, possibly because of the strong rainstorm that lasted all match. Cruz Azul looks likely to make if official in the return leg on Sunday. The 1st half started under incredibly rainy conditions. A run by Omar Campos ended with a dangerous cross into the area but Leon’s goalkeeper, Oscar Garcia, would get to the ball before a Cruz Azul attacker could reach it. After getting the ball in the area, Jose Paradela got off a left footed shot that went past Garcia to score and give Cruz Azul the 1-0 lead. Nicolas Ibañez got off a left footed shot in the area that forced a good save from Garcia. The match started to suffer as Leon tried to go on offense while Cruz Azul defended and counter, but neither team did either well on the wet conditions. Diber Cambindo went on a 1 vs 1 but his shot was blocked by Cruz Azul’s goalkeeper, Andres Gudiño, who made a good save. From outside the area, Nicolas Ibañez would get off a right footed shot that was deflected past Garcia and into the net to score and give Cruz Azul the 2-0 lead. Without being overly superior, Cruz Azul was once again very efficient and had a two goal lead with their few opportunities. A great pass in the area to Jeremy Marquez was wasted when he took too long to get off a shot and the ball was cleared. A shot from outside the area by Cambindo was blocked and would eventually easily reach Gudiño because of it. Off a free kick, a cross into the area was terribly cleared by Gudiño, which would fall to Sebastian Vega, but his close range chance was blocked by defender Willer Ditta. The halftime whistle blew as Cruz Azul looked like they were in control of the match and the series. The 2nd half started with Leon subbing Fernando Beltran, Ismael Diaz and Fernando Valadez for Juan Pablo Dominguez, Jose Alvarado and Jose Ivan Rodriguez. Ibañez got the ball in the area and got off a turn around right footed shot that forced a good save from Garcia. A left footed shot from outside the area by Erik Lira was saved by Garcia. Ibañez got the ball in the area for a 1 vs 1 but as he tried to get past Garcia, he would lose the ball to the goalkeeper. A cross into the area was headed from close range by Alvarado but the ball went wide. Cruz Azul subbed out Nicolas Ibañez, Carlos Rodriguez and Jeremy Marquez for Gabriel Fernandez, Carlos Rotondi and Alan Mozo. Leon subbed out Ivan Moreno for Edgar G

item.title: US Merchant Marine Academy looking to make more history in Division III football playoffs
item.description: They’re sea-sing the day at the United States Merchant Marine Academy. It’s a historic year for the 8-1 Mariners, who will play in the second round of the Division III football playoffs for the first time in Kings Point history. “It’s really a special team and how close-knit they are,” head coach Jameson Croall told The Post. “Really, when times get difficult … we lean on each other and respond to that adversity together.” A U.S. Merchant Marine Academy player runs up field during his team’s 42-14 blowout win over the Coast Guard Academy on Nov. 14, 2026, in the Secretaries’ Cup at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. Matt Kaminsky/ZUMA Press Wire The Mariners face No. 25 Hampden-Sydney on the road Saturday at noon after a first-round bye. The USMMA returns to the playoffs for the first time since 1994, the academy’s only other berth. It’s a unique situation for midshipmen on the team who were slated to begin their term at sea — where they can be deployed anywhere around the globe — right after the regular season ended. Several players are spending their mornings on the academy’s flagship vessel, the Kings Pointer, as an interim solution while they wait for long-term stationing after the playoffs. They come back to land and practice in the evening, ready to work, Croall said. “Their ability to compartmentalize all of those things and be able to focus on what they need to focus on in the moment is really a pretty special quality that I think embodies our team. “We really don’t have many bad practices.” The Mariners have also been sailing to victory thanks to dual-threat junior quarterback Bubba Mustain, who averaged 100 rushing yards per game and threw for 16 touchdowns in nine weeks. “He’s really just a complete player with a team around him that’s fully bought in and able to make plays for him as well.”

item.title: King Rice opens up on absence from UNC basketball, emotional return | Exclusive
item.description: CHAPEL HILL — The emotions didn’t fully hit King Rice until he returned to the visiting locker room at the Smith Center following a 40-point loss to his alma mater. Rice, 57, certainly wasn’t pleased with Monmouth’s performance in an 85-45 defeat to North Carolina . But after nearly 500 games as the Hawks’ head coach over 16 seasons, he knows wins and losses come and go. What lingered was bigger than results. More than 40 years of memories and relationships came flooding back when Rice saw who was waiting for him after the game. MALONE'S PATH: Michael Malone goes from practice ejection to lifelong loyalty at Seton Hall Prep | Exclusive UNC BASKETBALL REUNION: The moment at UNC's basketball reunion that caught Michael Malone off guard Former UNC guard Kenny Smith was there. So were former Tar Heels assistant coaches Phil Ford and Dave Hanners. Dave Blaha, a former walk-on who often gave Rice rides home to upstate New York during their playing days, was there too. Rice hadn’t seen Blaha since the 1990s. “That’s when it got emotional for me,” Rice said during a 20-minute conversation with The Fayetteville Observer. “Because I didn’t play with Kenny. Obviously, Coach Ford coached me and helped me grow up a whole bunch. But then Coach Hanners came in there and said, ‘Listen to this guy. He cares about y’all, he loves y’all. I know he yells and uses curse words sometimes, but he’s trying to get y’all to do the right things. It’s all from the right place.’ ” It was a special moment because, as Rice mentioned, "those guys are Carolina men and they came to support me" at the Smith Center. “They know I don’t like losing like that. They know that crushed everything in my being, but you got to be a man, you got to stand up. This isn’t the first time I’ve gotten my butt kicked, it’s not going to be the last time I get my butt kicked," Rice said. “But, as a man, you got to stand up. Your friends are still there for you. Even though I didn’t play with those guys, they came to support and that’s where my kids can learn the most from. It’s bigger than basketball. Yeah, we got whupped (Monday), but it’s bigger than basketball and the experience was great for us. We’ll be better because of how that game went.” A loss is temporary. Family is forever. Why King Rice stayed away, eventually returned to UNC A four-year player for Dean Smith and the Tar Heels from 1987-91, Rice scored 861 points, dished out 629 assists and racked up 147 steals. He helped the program win two ACC Tournament championships and, as a captain in 1991, made the Final Four. Even after a long absence — including 10 years between games in Chapel Hill — and what Rice described as “some hurt feelings,” he returned to Chapel Hill for a UNC basketball reunion in October before Monmouth’s Nov. 23 game against the Tar Heels. UNC hosted Monmouth in 2012 and 2016 under Roy Williams, but Rice said he hadn’t been back to the Smith Center in a “long time” before he attended the reunion with his wife and two

item.title: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — The Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Linebacker Jared "Bird" Lloyd was named the 2026 Media Player of the Year on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The Media Player of the Year award had been given to the top Bears player from 1982-2017 and was revived in 2026. “This means a lot. I really appreciate you guys covering me and I’m very appreciative of you guys just getting my name out there more,” Lloyd said. “You guys reporting on me, doesn’t just help me. It helps my teammates, it helps the university and it helps the football program.” Missouri State football: Bears snag its top in-state recruit in the program's history Entering the final game of the season, Lloyd leads the nation with 127 total tackles. He also ranks No. 1 in tackles per game with 11.55. This is the best season by a Missouri State player since 2016, when Dylan Cole set the mark. This is the third-most tackles in a single Missouri State season since 2004. Lloyd also has two sacks, one forced fumble and three pass deflections. The Daytona Beach, Florida, native will finish his career with more than 275 tackles in his five seasons in Springfield. “Bird will go down in history as one of the most important players in Missouri State football history, shepherding this team into the FBS era. He has been one of the best tacklers in college football in 2026,” the News-Leader's Liam Keating said in a press release. “Instead of competing for individual accolades, he's always been a team-first player. This is what makes him a special player and worthy of the first media-given award in almost a decade.” Lloyd is the seventh linebacker to win the award. Ken Braden (1986), Matt Soraghan (’87), James Turnage (’88), DeLaun Fowler (’94-95), P.J. Jones (’01) and Cole (’15-16) were named winners. Missouri State: How star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era "There's something satisfying about seeing the fruits of one's labor play out before your very eyes," Collingwood said. "Lloyd made a concerted effort to get leaner and quicker in the offseason, and it's translated into him being the country's most prolific tackler. Between his hard work, matter-of-fact disposition, productivity, and rare five-year allegiance to the same school, Lloyd is certainly deserving of this award." Missouri State (4-7, 3-4 CUSA) will host No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0) at 1 p.m. for senior day on Saturday, Nov. 28. This will be Lloyd’s final game representing the Bears inside Plaster Stadium. Keating and the Daily Citizen’s Ryan Collingwood voted on the winner. Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. Send stats or information to him at Lkeating@usatodayco.com This article originally appeared on Springfield News-Leader: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year

item.title: KJ Duff reflects on Rutgers football legacy as his NFL decision looms
item.description: PISCATAWAY – All KJ Duff knew at the time was that he couldn’t finish the rest of the game. Rutgers football’s star wide receiver had reaggravated an injury during the Scarlet Knights ’ game against Michigan that he had suffered the week prior, but even as he walked off the SHI Stadium field the possibility he had played his last snap never crossed his mind. Then came the diagnosis of a high-ankle sprain, followed by surgery that would end his season four games too soon. “It definitely was frustrating,” Duff told USA TODAY-New Jersey this week. “All I really want to do is play football, and then that gets taken away.” Frustrating for Duff. Disappointing for the program. And perhaps more disappointing for a fanbase that, for three seasons, watched Duff develop into one of the best receivers in the program’s history, climbing lists in the record books, filling highlight reels with jaw-dropping catches and cementing a legacy that won’t soon be forgotten. Duff hasn’t officially announced his future – whether he’ll pursue the NFL or return to Rutgers for his final year of eligibility. But Duff is projected as a potential first-round draft pick. He’d become the first Rutgers player to hold that distinction since 2010. Coach Greg Schiano also said after a recent game that if Duff asked him, he’d advise him to pursue the NFL. If Duff makes that choice, Schiano made it clear he’ll miss having him in the program. The reasons why are clear. “I’ve told everybody that comes here, it was a lot of fun while it lasted because our hardest working player was our best player,” Schiano said. “That’s fun when you can point to him as an example. Especially in this era of so many newcomers, like, ‘Look what he’s doing, Try to do that.’” That work paid off. “It feels great to be recognized as that, but it's really about what you put into it,” Duff said. “I go with that mentality of, ‘I want to be great.’ I want to put myself in the best position to be successful.” Duff said his focus now is on getting healthy, which was off to a good start just more than two weeks after surgery. Duff said he was already doing some jogging and his doctors said he’s ahead of schedule in his recovery after initially saying he’d be able to resume football activities in January. “I don't want to rush anything and put myself in a bad position,” Duff said. KJ Duff stayed loyal to Rutgers football and developed into a star receiver Duff, who joined the program as the top overall recruit in New York for the 2024 recruiting class out of St. Anthony's High School on Long Island, in three seasons at Rutgers had 132 catches for 2,283 yards with 17 touchdowns. In eight games this season before getting hurt, Duff had 774 receiving yards on 45 catches with a season-high nine touchdowns. He had at least 100 receiving yards in four of those games. He ranks seventh in program history in career yards and is tied for fifth in touchdowns and 10 th in receptions. Duff established his legacy – doing that only

item.title: Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea: Prediction, betting tips and lineups
item.description: Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea tips: A score draw - 7/2 BetVictor Liam Delap to score - 23/10 SpreadEx Chelsea make the trip north to Nottingham Forest tonight, aiming to put the disappointment of back-to-back defeats to Sunderland and Leeds behind them (kick-off 8pm, live on Sky Sports). Xabi Alonso’s side went down 1-0 at the Stadium of Light before they were thrashed 4-1 at home by Leeds last weekend despite taking the lead. That was their fifth Premier League defeat in 11 games, leaving them eighth in the table and five points off the top four. Their opponents tonight have also had a tough start to the season with just two wins so far, which means they are outside the bottom three on goal difference only. One of those wins came against Manchester City a fortnight ago when Liam Delap scored twice to help his side to a shock 3-1 win and ended a five-game winless run. Both managers are under increasing pressure in their new roles, but it is Oliver Glasner, who is the favourite on betting sites to be the next manager to lose his job at 11/8, and he will know that the patience of Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis will only last so long. Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction tips: The only thing we expect is goals The two sides have met 102 times, and Chelsea lead the head-to-head 43 wins to 28. This will only be the 19th meeting in the Premier League, though and in those games the Blues have won just seven to Forest’s five, while the remaining six have been drawn. The strange statistic between these sides is that both have better away records, with Chelsea winning the last three matches at the City Ground, while Forest have won two and drawn two of the last four at Stamford Bridge. Last season, Josh Acheampong, Pedro Neto and Reece James were on target in a 3-0 win at Forest, before Malo Gusto was sent off three minutes before the end. In the return match in the capital in May, Taiwo Awoniyi scored twice to help his side to a 3-1 win, which went a long way to helping preserve their Premier League status. Forest’s last home win against tonight’s opponents came way back in 1997 when Stuart Pearce and the late Chris Bart-Williams scored in a 2-0 win. Based on those stats, it’s a surprise that football betting sites have Forest as the favourites for the win at 8/5, while you can get 9/5 on Chelsea to take all three points. The Blues have scored 20 so far and conceded the same amount, so we expect goals, and you can get 3/4 on over 2.5 goals and 8/13 on both teams to score, but with both teams so out of form, we’re going for a draw. Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction 1: A score draw - 7/2 Bet Victor Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea prediction: Delap to come back to haunt Chelsea After enduring a disappointing spell at Stamford Bridge, striker Liam Delap would love to get one over his former club tonight. The 23-year-old scored just one Premier League goal for the Blues last season, in 18 appearances, and he’s already improved on that number for Forest.

item.title: The Bayern Insider: Crucial Musiala meeting held as Olise concern emerges behind the scenes
item.description: The Bayern Insider: Crucial Musiala meeting held as Olise concern emerges behind the scenes Welcome to today’s exclusive & comprehensive round-up of all things Bayern Munich from Bayern insider Christian Falk. Featuring updates on Jamal Musiala, Michael Olise, Joshua Kimmich, and Donyell Malen. Today’s top stories What is the latest on the Jamal Musiala situation? Could Nicolò Tresoldi be signed in the January transfer window? Is Derry Scherhant a potential option to cover Luis Diaz? And plenty more on Max Eberl, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, Jonathan Tah & Min-jae Kim For everyone following our work here on CF Bayern Insider, you’ll know how close you are to the inner workings of this football club, because it was again our exclusive that delved into the Jamal Musiala story. We had a photo of the secret meeting at Säbener Straße on Tuesday, and we knew what happened there. Before, we heard about Uli Hoeneß talking about a need to potentially discuss the salary; CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen spoke along similar lines… and then there was Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who spoke in an interview after the match against FC Köln. It’s an interesting situation, as he wasn’t in the mixed zone like the other Bayern bosses. The cameras were coming up to him in the stands. It wasn’t really spontaneous. It was absolutely planned and the message was really direct, certainly more direct than the messages we’ve seen before from the other bosses. He was saying that Bayern don’t know if they can sell Jamal Musiala and they weren’t sure if anyone follows this player anymore, as he doesn’t have a market value anymore. The club believes that it has to talk with Musiala’s side now, because for 12 days they’ve talked about the footballer but not directly with his entourage. With this in mind, we knew there had to be a meeting taking place, and we were there! Want more CF Bayern Insider coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust In the end, Vincent Kompany, Christoph Freund, and Max Eberl – this side of Bayern Munich – have always been in talks with the Musiala side, and they know how he’s feeling, how the treatment is going, if he’s improving, whether he’ll be on the pitch, and so on. But not all of the bosses are so clearly informed. This is why it was so important that this meeting Säbener Straße took place and the bosses were at the table. Jan-Christian Dreesen, Herbert Hainer – on one hand the CEO, on the other the president – and Eberl were there in talks with Jamal Musiala’s team. They told him that not everyone is thinking about the situation like some people are speaking about it. They want the best for the playmaker. They also don’t want to talk about the salary right now. Bayern also released a press release to confirm talks and that they were aware of the medication and what will happen in the future, and they don’t want to put pressure on him. item.title: Carlos Alcaraz claimed to have made a change to his game inspired by Pete Sampras ahead of 2027
item.description: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself the best player in the world, having strolled to major titles or beaten his rivals with minimal fuss. Normally, that could encourage complacency, and he would have been forgiven for occasionally succumbing to that notion. However, that has yet to happen. Every time it feels like the 23-year-old simply cannot get any better, he manages it, with his current run of form no different. Carlos Alcaraz spent nearly five months sidelined due to injury this year, but even that has not prevented him from improving a key area of his game, which has now been compared to one of the sport’s greatest-ever players. Carlos Alcaraz discusses his changes to his serve Alcaraz’s serve has been a much-discussed topic for years now. After all, if a weakness had to be selected in the Spaniard’s game, this used to be it, with it more than capable, but far from a lethal weapon. Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images Then, last year, he served his way to US Open glory once again, reaching the final without dropping a set and getting broken just three times en route to the title. Even that was not enough, with Alcaraz reportedly having made further tweaks to this all-important shot. According to Marca , the latest changes are inspired by Pete Sampras, one of the greatest servers in tennis history, with particular focus on his raised foot movement during the motion. Samu Lopez, his coach, added: “We were looking for him to have more balance at the beginning of the movement, and that would help him to be more fluid and that he could push himself upwards.” Then, at a Davis Cup press conference earlier this week, Alcaraz directly addressed these changes, admitting: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. 🎙️Carlos on his serve improvements: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. “I don't usually look at stats during practice. I do… https://t.co/BK02s8kU8T pic.twitter.com/cT7b0gk1kt — Alcaraz Daily (@alcarazdaily) November 26, 2026 “I don’t usually look at stats during practice. I do look at them after matches, because they matter for the next round. We know how important the serve is. It’s something we’ve improved and put a lot of focus on. “Since the US Open, this is the hardest I’ve worked on my serve. Accuracy was a big part of it, and we’ve worked on it more because I’m not very tall and can’t serve like some other players.” Earlier this year, Alcaraz’s serve was accused of ‘not doing enough damage’ . It’s incredible how he has managed to combat those complaints despite spending so long out injured with a wrist injury.

item.title: Barcelona’s unlikely goal machine is starting to make his case
item.description: Barcelona’s unlikely goal machine is starting to make his case Gabriel Jesus has made an encouraging start to life at Barcelona, scoring five goals in just 376 minutes despite struggling to secure regular playing time. The Brazilian striker arrived at Spotify Camp Nou to take over Robert Lewandowski’s place, but has found opportunities limited by Raphinha’s remarkable form in the centre forward position. While expectations were modest compared with those surrounding Lewandowski, Jesus is beginning to show why Barcelona brought him to the club. His goalscoring return has been particularly impressive considering he has made only 11 appearances and had not completed a full match before the Champions League fixture against Sabah in Baku. Gabriel Jesus scores whenever Flick starts him One of the most striking aspects of Jesus’ Barcelona career so far is his record when selected from the beginning. The striker has scored in all three matches in which Hansi Flick has started him, finding the net against Getafe, Real Betis and Sabah. Gabriel Jesus has scored five goals in very limited time for Barcelona. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His goal in Baku came from close range , with Jesus reacting quickly to a loose ball inside the penalty area. It was not a spectacular finish, but it still showed the instinctive positioning that has become a feature of his performances. As such, the Brazilian has scored five goals in 376 minutes, which translates to a goal every 76 minutes. Barcelona have discovered a natural finisher Jesus, who signed from Arsenal, has already shown different ways of scoring during his short Barcelona spell, having demonstrated quality in the air, the ability to finish with either foot, a powerful strike and composure when opportunities arrive inside the box. His greatest strength, however, may be his anticipation. Jesus regularly positions himself to react before defenders, allowing him to convert chances that might otherwise disappear. Gabriel Jesus has scored the same amount og goals as Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Mind you, his five goals also match the totals of Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi, despite both players having enjoyed considerably more playing time. Raphinha’s form limits his opportunities Meanwhile, it is clear that Raphinha’s extraordinary run of 19 goals in 16 matches has made it difficult for Jesus to establish himself as Barcelona’s first choice in attack. The Brazilian winger has excelled as a centre forward, a development that even surprised Raphinha himself. Jesus still needs to improve his understanding with teammates including Fermin Lopez, Pedri, Lamine Yamal and Gordon as he adapts to Barcelona’s style, but that will improve as the season moves on. For now, however, his numbers provide a compelling argument for greater involvement. Five goals from limited opportunities suggest that Barcelona have a striker capable of making an immediate impact whenever Flick turns to

item.title: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine
item.description: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine As we near the halfway point of the season, it is safe to say that Kylian Mbappe has emerged as one of the best performers in Europe. The Frenchman has continued his goalscoring exploits at Santiago Bernabeu, having racked up as many as 19 goals across all competitions. Mbappe has looked quite fit in doing so as well, as he has played in every single one of Real Madrid’s matches so far, leading the club to believe that the player is at the peak of his physical performance. Mbappe’s bid to win Ballon d’Or Mbappe has embraced the number nine role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Given the sheer productivity Mbappe has provided to the table at Real Madrid this season, it goes without saying that he will once again be one of the candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. Keeping that in mind, El Chiringuito has recently claimed that Mbappe himself is aware of the fact that he has more chances of winning the Ballon d’Or if he continues to operate as a number nine. This comes against the backdrop of earlier allegations against Mbappe that he enjoys operating more as a left-winger. In the months since, Mbappe has now fully embraced the role of a number nine, and this has been quite evident in his performances this season. Although the Frenchman still has the tendency to drift out wide, he has done so far less frequently in recent weeks and his overall combination play with other attackers has improved tenfold. Real Madrid, as a result, have dominated their opponents. Can Mbappe win the Ballon d’Or? Mbappe finished second in the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Mbappe’s numbers so far this season make it obvious that he will be one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. However, the Frenchman’s fate will once again depend on whether or not Real Madrid can secure any silverware this season. Los Blancos have not won a single major trophy in two seasons, so breaking that rut could go a long way in boosting Mbappe’s chances of winning his first Ballon d’Or. Fortunately, with Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid now have a seasoned coach who has shown exceptional decision-making skills and has the technical know-how in competitions such as the Champions League. Mbappe, to that end, will play an integral part of Mourinho’s war machine as they look to break Real Madrid’s trophy rut during the second half of the campaign.

item.title: PSG is now a serious contenders to Arsenal for La Liga star
item.description: PSG is now a serious contenders to Arsenal for La Liga star Nico Williams remains one of the most highly regarded wingers in world football, and Arsenal continue to be linked with a move for the Spaniard as they look to strengthen their squad further. The Gunners already have one of the strongest teams in Europe, but they are not prepared to become complacent and continue to monitor opportunities to improve their options. Williams remains on their radar as a potential addition who could bring further quality to their attack. His situation at Athletic Club is particularly interesting because, despite committing his future to the club until 2035, his contract includes a release clause that could allow him to leave if an interested team meets the required conditions. That clause offers encouragement to Arsenal as they consider whether to pursue a deal. However, the Gunners are far from alone in their interest, with several of Europe’s leading sides reportedly keen to add the winger to their squads. PSG emerge as Arsenal competition One of the clubs that could challenge Arsenal for Williams is Paris Saint-Germain. The French champions are also interested in securing his services, potentially setting up competition between two clubs with the financial resources to pursue a significant transfer. According to Fichajes , PSG are serious about beating Arsenal to the Spaniard’s signature. Their reported interest adds another complication for the Gunners, who would have to compete with other major European teams if they decide to make a formal approach. Williams remains happy at Athletic Club, meaning Arsenal and their rivals cannot assume that he is already looking for a way out. His current commitment to the Spanish side makes any potential transfer dependent on both his wishes and the opportunities available to him. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) Williams’ future remains open The winger was previously keen on joining Barcelona, showing that he has considered the possibility of moving to another major club. That interest suggests he could eventually become open to a new challenge, although there is no certainty about when he might decide to leave Athletic Club. Arsenal will therefore need to remain attentive to developments surrounding his future. Their interest could become more complicated if additional clubs make their intentions clear and begin competing for his signature. If Williams eventually decides that he wants to leave Spain, the Gunners will have to contend with growing competition from some of the biggest clubs in European football. item.title: Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 in Australia despite hitting ‘the worst shot’ he has ever hit as a pro
item.description: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey. The 33-year-old Australian carded seven birdies and an eagle during his second round at The Lakes on Friday. Cam Smith is now sitting just four shots adrift of the leader, Nicolai von Dellingshausen, with 36 holes left to play. Smith is looking to win his fourth Australian PGA Championship this week, and if he carries on playing like he did on Friday across the weekend, he will have a great chance to do just that. Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 at the Australian PGA Smith wasn’t entirely happy with his opening round in Australia on Thursday, so he would have been delighted to see such drastic improvements on day two. The former LIV Golf star spoke to reporters after shooting a second-round 64 and responded when asked to give his verdict on his current form. “Yeah, I think so, it’s definitely going to be a different year. I’m excited. I haven’t done the European stuff before, and just starting at home is pretty special,” Smith said. “I got in a bit of a groove and rhythm today, which is what we’ve been looking for. We’ve been searching for that and it finally kind of all came together today.” However, not everything went swimmingly for Smith. The 2022 Open champion hit what he described as probably the worst shot he has ever hit as a professional on the par-three 15th hole. However, after leaving himself a full wedge shot into the green, he holed a 25-foot putt to salvage his par. “That might have been the worst shot I’ve ever hit as a professional,” said Smith. “It wasn’t a shank, but it was close. It definitely kind of kept the momentum going, for sure.” Cam Smith will be hoping to avoid any more card-wrecking shots like the one he hit on the 15th hole on Friday. If he manages to post two rounds in the 60s over the weekend, he may well have a chance of winning the fourth Australian PGA Championship of his career.

item.title: Scott McTominay: Ex-Man United ace makes major decision on January Napoli exit
item.description: Scott McTominay: Ex-Man United ace makes major decision on January Napoli exit Manchester United’s plans to immediately bring Scott McTominay back to Old Trafford appear to have hit a standstill. The midfield was at the centre of INEOS’ squad rebuild this summer, but their investment has yet to bear fruit. The Red Devils spent over €150 million on Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans, but the trio have hardly improved the team. Tielemans has been heavily involved, while Santos has been in and out of the starting XI. Baleba , meanwhile, remains sidelined with a hamstring injury after already missing the beginning of the campaign with an ankle issue. With United languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table after 11 games, new manager Mauricio Pochettino could seek further reinforcements in midfield in 2027. Recent reports suggest that the Red Devils have been offered the chance to re-sign their former academy graduate McTominay next year. McTominay has been a hit in Serie A United made the surprise decision to allow McTominay to leave Old Trafford in the summer of 2024, and it has since been proven to be a poor move. The Scottish midfielder has hit a higher gear since moving to Napoli, helping them win Serie A in his debut campaign. McTominay has continued his upward trajectory with the Italian club and has already scored 33 goals and registered 10 assists in 93 appearances across competitions. For the record, the 29-year-old, who rose through the ranks at Old Trafford, has 29 goals and eight assists in 255 appearances for the Red Devils in his career. However, with the player’s contract set to expire in 2028 and a renewal yet to materialise, he has been linked with an exit from the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that the player would prefer to return to Old Trafford rather than join Chelsea, who are also in the race. It was suggested that McTominay’s camp held a meeting with Napoli sporting director Giovanni Manna to discuss his future. However, an update on the saga has now emerged that could complicate matters for United. Scott McTominay: 2026/27 Stats Napoli · 2026/27 Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 McTominay unlikely to leave Napoli in January According to Il Mattino , as cited by Sport Witness , McTominay has no desire to leave Napoli in January, and this was communicated in the meeting with Manna. While the development certainly puts a dent in United’s plans, it does not effectively rule out a move next summer. McTominay’s renewal remains a complicated affair, especially given the finances involved. If the Scot does not sign a new deal by the end of this season, the Red Devils could have the chance to bring their prodigal son home. item.title: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record
item.description: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record Bournemouth are already dreaming on European glory under Marco Rose, and rightly so. After going 1-0 down against Celta Vigo in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night, having a man sent off and then scoring two goals, the Cherries’ 2-1 victory is their fifth straight win in their maiden European competition. With five wins from five and maximum points, Bournemouth became the first English team, and only the third in history, to win their first five European matches. Only Nuremberg (1961/62) and Ararat Yerevan (1972/73) are the only other teams to record such a feat. It was also their tenth straight victory across all competitions – a record matched only by Real Madrid. Speaking to the BBC Sport after Bournemouth’s latest victory, Rose, formerly of Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, said: “Dreaming is always allowed. When you participate in a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible result.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Eastleigh to keep Hill, Bristow & Bartram in charge
item.description: Richard Hill is in his fourth spell in charge of Eastleigh, having guided them to promotion to the National League in 2014 [Shutterstock] Eastleigh have confirmed that Richard Hill, Jason Bristow and Vince Bartram will continue to oversee first-team affairs for the foreseeable future. The trio have been in charge of the side on an interim basis since Matt Gray was sacked earlier this month. Former manager Hill had conducted post-match media affairs after Eastleigh's past two games - a 3-1 win at Tamworth and a 3-1 home loss to Yeovil Town. The club had won just one of their final eight matches under Gray and are currently 18th in the National League. The news comes days after owner Stewart Donald confirmed to fans he will leave the club at the end of the season. "Given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the club's ownership, the board believes it is right to manage the first team within our existing resources," a statement released by Eastleigh read. "Our priority remains securing our place in the National League. "We also want to put together a strong run in the FA Trophy and carry that momentum into our league performances." The club has also confirmed Gray's assistant Jason Goodliffe has left the Spitfires by mutual consent.

item.title: Marco Rose hails 'relentless' Bournemouth after 10-man Cherries make European history against Celta Vigo
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CELTA VIGO-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose could not hide his admiration for his players after witnesssing a truly historic European night at the Vitality Stadium. Despite falling a goal behind and being reduced to ten men, the Cherries produced a stunning turnaround to defeat Celta Vigo 2-1 and cement their growing reputation on the continent. Cherries roar back to sink Celta Bournemouth’s incredible transformation under Rose reached new heights on Thursday as the Premier League side secured their tenth consecutive victory in all competitions. Facing a difficult trip to Celta in the Europa League league phase, the Cherries appeared to be heading toward a frustrating evening after Bafode Diaktie was sent off during the first half. With a goal deficit to overcome and a player short, the odds were stacked heavily against the visitors. However, a spirited second-half performance saw Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan find the net to turn the game on its head. The manager was quick to credit the psychological fortitude of his players, who refused to accept defeat despite the circumstances. "What a team, what a spirit, what an energy,” the German manager said following the final whistle. “I’m really proud after being one player less, 1-0 down,” he told BBC Radio Solent . Tactical flexibility and individual brilliance The comeback was not just a product of willpower but also significant tactical adjustments that Rose implemented to balance the side after the red card. One of the standout performers in this regard was David Brooks, who was asked to fill a defensive void that few expected him to master. The versatility shown by the Welsh international allowed the Cherries to maintain their shape while still posing a threat on the counter-attack during the second period. Rose admitted that the victory was less about rigid systems and more about the players' ability to step up in difficult moments. "I said to Ty (Tyler Adams), sometimes it’s not about tactics and formations and stuff like this," Rose explained. "Brooksy did a great job when we got one player less, he played just right defender like he played it for 10 years. We changed in the right moment, everyone did his job on a really high level." Momentum shifts and belief The turning point arrived shortly after the interval when Bournemouth found their equalizer, a goal that completely altered the psychological dynamic of the match. With the scores level, the English side seemed to find a second wind, pressing Celta high up the pitch despite their numerical disadvantage. Rose highlighted that the early goal in the second half was the catalyst for the relentless pressure that eventually led to the winner. "We created the momentum after the half-time with the first goal and we were just relentless," the former RB Leipzig boss added. The manager noted that the squad’s conviction was the deciding factor: "We never stopped to believe in this win and that’s why big, big, big congratu

item.title: Who is in the running for BBC Men's Footballer of the Year?
item.description: [BBC] Voting has closed for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year. Fans from the UK have been voting from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal. The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December. Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate. "Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game. "It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner." The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game. The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales). Read more on the five contenders below. Jude Bellingham Age: 23 Country: England Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament. In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway. That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958. Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player. The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts. Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe [Getty Images] Harry Kane Age: 33 Country: England Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer. His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12. item.title: Why Cambridgeshire derby could be season-defining
item.description: Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road [Getty Images] History, tradition, bragging rights. Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT). Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads. At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season. As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift. 'It's all about winning' The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's. They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline. Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990. Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record. "We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said. "We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter. "It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game." The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February. "This game is at the top of the mountain," he said. "No doubt about it. The players will be up for it, we've shown them videos of the previous games, we've got fans sending messages. "We're doing everything we can to make them realise how big this game is. It's not another game, it's the derby. A great game. "Neil knows what it means. We're two passionate managers. He's done far better than me as a manager so far, so hats off to him. But we both want to win. "They will bring 1,600 fans and we need to show Cambridge that we want to county to be blue." While this derby is new territory for Savage, Harris comes armed with the memory of defeat in his only previous taste of the tie in a season than ultimately ended with relegation for the U's. item.title: Gasly amused by Verstappen and Russell feud: 'I'm just eating my popcorn'
item.description: Pierre Gasly has weighed in on the latest chapter of the bitter rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell , admitting that he is thoroughly enjoying watching the drama unfold from the sidelines. Tensions between Verstappen and Russell resurfaced during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend following an on-track altercation in the third and final free practice session, during which the pair made contact. The incident reignited a rivalry that reached boiling point at the end of the 2024 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, when the two drivers publicly traded accusations following a controversial qualifying incident in Lusail. Verstappen added further fuel to the fire following his victory in Las Vegas, claiming that Russell was "so far below my level" and remarking that "karma is a bi**h" following the Mercedes driver's difficult evening. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Russell was subsequently given the opportunity to respond to the Dutchman's remarks ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, describing the situation as unnecessary. The Mercedes driver stood by his criticism of Verstappen following their practice clash but insisted that he had no intention of prolonging their feud, acknowledging that he might have been too open when speaking to the media. Verstappen, meanwhile, refused to be drawn into another exchange of words with his rival during his media commitments in Qatar, insisting that everything that needed to be said off track had already been said. Gasly enjoys watching Verstappen and Russell's rivalry unfold The ongoing feud has also attracted the attention of several other drivers on the grid, including Gasly, who briefly partnered Verstappen at Red Bull in 2019 and has known both drivers since childhood. The Alpine driver admitted that he was enjoying the spectacle, suggesting that neither the altercation in Las Vegas nor the subsequent war of words came as a surprise to him: "Not the first time, not the last time these two are going to go at it. From my side I'm just sitting and eating my popcorn laughing about it." Gasly also offered an insight into how he approaches disagreements with his former teammate, explaining that he prefers to address any issues directly with the Dutchman. "I think it was best with Max just to tell him right up in his face! He's someone that just takes anything," the Frenchman told Sky Sports. "You can have opinions, etcetera. I like both of them, obviously [they are] very different. We all know each other, we know each other since we were kids."

item.title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
item.description: Australia won the 2017-18 Ashes series against England 4-0 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense". However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events. "All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said. "While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied. "Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials." The forum will be open for six weeks. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," CA chair David Boon said. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. "It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." Khawaja hinted the team

item.title: From fuel subsidy return to Ajaokuta revival, Atiku’s 2027 promises so far
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, tackle insecurity, create jobs and revive key infrastructure projects if elected president in 2027. The African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate has made the pledges at campaign rallies in Sokoto, Bauchi, Yobe and Kogi states, while presenting his proposed policies as measures to reduce the cost of living and improve economic conditions. At the ADC presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto on November 4 , Atiku promised to restore petrol subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders to encourage trade and tackle insecurity, including kidnapping, banditry and terrorism. He also pledged to reduce the cost of pilgrimage for Muslim and Christian faithful. Atiku said restoring petrol subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of essential goods. He also argued that reopening the land borders would benefit farmers, traders and transport operators by stimulating cross-border commerce. At a rally in Bauchi State on November 14, Atiku extended his subsidy promise to electricity, saying he would restore both petroleum and electricity subsidies if elected. He also pledged to strengthen security, particularly in the North-East, resume oil exploration in the Kolmani field and continue the Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project. “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue,” he said at the Bauchi rally. At a campaign rally in Yobe State on November 15, Atiku again promised to restore petrol and electricity subsidies, while pledging to address insecurity and create employment opportunities for young Nigerians. “Let me assure you that once I am elected president in 2027, I will bring back the fuel subsidy,” he said, adding that he would also restore electricity subsidy. He further promised that his administration would work to ensure peace returned to Yobe and other parts of the country, and that young Nigerians would have access to employment opportunities. In Kogi State on November 24 , Atiku campaigned on an “Affordable Life” message, promising to reduce fuel costs, support local production and improve Nigerians’ purchasing power. He said his proposals were aimed at easing the pressure on households, workers and small businesses. At the rally in Lokoja, he also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill through foreign investment, without relying on government funding for the project. He promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger to enable the port to serve other states and create employment opportunities. “I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. This is very doable because we can bring in foreign investment to complete that without

item.title: ILT20: Sherfane Rutherford's explosive fifty powers MI Emirates to 36-run win over Abu Dhabi Knight Riders
item.description: MI Emirates registered their second win of ILT20 Season 5 after beating Abu Dhabi Knight Riders by 36 runs at the Zayed Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Sherfane Rutherford produced a stunning batting display, scoring 51 off just 18 balls, while Nicholas Pooran remained unbeaten on 42 off 33 deliveries. Their efforts helped MI Emirates post a massive 207/4 in 20 overs. The bowlers then stepped up to restrict the Knight Riders to 171/7. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Zahoor Khan picked up two wickets each, while Rashid Khan kept things tight with figures of 1/13. Sunil Narine was the standout bowler for the Knight Riders, taking 1/11, including a maiden. Rutherford, Pooran power MI Emirates to 207 After being asked to bat first, MI Emirates got off to a flying start. Openers Kusal Perera and Muhammad Waseem attacked the bowling and added 77 runs for the first wicket in 52 balls. Perera scored 33 off 23 balls, while Waseem contributed 41 off 37 deliveries. The opening pair helped MI Emirates reach 57 without loss in the powerplay. Sunil Narine provided the Knight Riders with their first breakthrough in the ninth over when he dismissed Perera, who was caught behind. Abdullah Tarakhail, making his ILT20 debut, then struck twice to bring his team back into the contest. The Afghanistan pacer removed Waseem and Tajinder Singh (10 off 8), leaving MI Emirates at 124/3. The scoring rate slowed down for a while, with MI Emirates managing just one run in the 17th over. However, Rutherford and Pooran changed the momentum with some powerful hitting. The pair collected 17 runs each in the 18th and 19th overs to take the score to 177/3. Rutherford then took the attack to Knight Riders captain Jason Holder in the final over. He smashed three consecutive sixes off the first three deliveries to bring up his half-century in just 17 balls. However, he was caught on the fourth delivery. Kieron Pollard joined Pooran in the middle and made an immediate impact, hitting two more sixes. He scored 12 off just two balls as MI Emirates finished with a massive 207/4. Holder had an expensive outing, conceding 62 runs in his four overs. The last three overs alone cost the Knight Riders 64 runs. Farooqi, Zahoor lead MI Emirates' bowling attack Chasing 208, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders began aggressively and collected 17 runs from Farooqi's opening over. However, the MI Emirates pacer bounced back quickly. He bowled Andre Fletcher (16 off 12) in the third over before dismissing Gulbadin Naib (5 off 6) in the fifth. The Knight Riders were reduced to 50/2. Zahoor Khan then removed Finn Allen (26 off 21) in the eighth over to put further pressure on the home team. Alishan Sharafu and Moeen Ali tried to revive the chase with a 45-run partnership off 27 balls. Both batters scored 36 runs, but Rashid Khan broke the stand by bowling Sharafu in the 13th over. Zahoor returned to dismiss Moeen in the 16th over, making the chase even tougher for the Knight Riders. Sunil Narine (4 off 15) retired out on the fin

item.title: ‘I nearly had a heart attack!’ - Thomas Frank celebrates first Crystal Palace win after dramatic Europa League comeback against Real Sociedad
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CRYSTAL PALACE-REAL SOCIEDAD - AFP Thomas Frank has tasted his first victory as Crystal Palace manager, but the Danish coach admitted the frantic closing stages of their 2-1 win over Real Sociedad left him fearing for his health. The Eagles came from behind at Selhurst Park to secure a vital Europa League result that could act as a catalyst for their season. Late goals and red card spark Selhurst Park turnaround Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr fired Real Sociedad ahead in the 66th minute of Frank's first home match, only for Jon Martin's second yellow card six minutes later to hand Palace a numerical advantage. Jean-Philippe Mateta converted from the penalty spot before Dwight McNeil poked home from fellow substitute Jorgen Strand Larsen's overhead kick. Unai Marrero saved Yeremy Pino's spot-kick, leaving goalkeeper Dean Henderson to make the last of his six stops against Orri Oskarsson late on. Frank hails brave attacking gamble after nervy finish Reflecting on bouncing back from Saturday's debut defeat to Coventry, Frank praised his squad's response to falling behind . “I think first and foremost to get it over the line, and [it was] an extremely important win for various reasons,” he said. “One, of course, confidence, and it relates to belief against an extremely good team. I think the first half we were compact and very disciplined in many ways. We missed the high-pressure situations we had, and I think we struggled to keep the ball well enough. “Second half I felt we were much better in the high pressure, and I felt we kept the ball much better. I actually felt we got a bit more momentum in the second half but then, out of the blue, they scored the 1-0 goal. But what I really like is the belief from the players, what they showed, and that we are threatening on set-pieces, we cannot underestimate that.” Frank also credited his bold substitutions once Real Sociedad went down to 10 men. “We know in football one moment can change the game,” he continued. “The penalty and the red card changed the game, then we still needed to score. To win still is important and we went brave, we went with the offensive substitutions and kept two strikers on the pitch, and that paid off. And then I think we were all close to getting a heart attack in the last five minutes.” European play-off boost offers hope amid relegation fight While Premier League survival remains the priority for the bottom-placed Eagles, Thursday's victory lifted them into the Europa League play-off spots, four places outside the top eight after five games. “I think we want to aim high,” the former Tottenham boss replied when asked about his continental ambitions. “We are ambitious for this tournament, and that’s why the win was so important.” Frank also agreed the comeback could prove a major turning point for his squad's morale. “That’s why it’s so important to keep doing the right things, keep believing, and keep going,” he said. item.title: Chiefs most to blame for Thanksgiving loss to Bills in ugly rainstorm
item.description: Chiefs most to blame for Thanksgiving loss to Bills in ugly rainstorm appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Kansas City Chiefs have spent the 2026 season feasting on inferior competition. Thanksgiving night in Orchard Park, though, exposed every flaw that separates them from the AFC’s true elite. In a driving rainstorm, Steve Spagnuolo’s defense delivered a masterclass. They held Josh Allen to 81 passing yards and two red-zone interceptions. Sadly, the Chiefs’ offense and special teams flushed it all away in a 13-10 walk-off loss . Tyler Bass drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired, but the game was lost long before that kick split the uprights. This was a self-inflicted wound of the highest order. The culprits are painfully obvious. Flawed contender Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Chiefs’ Week 12 showdown against the Bills was less a showcase of offensive fireworks and more an old-school trench war. It was dictated by sleet, swirling winds, and sloppy execution. Spagnuolo’s defense did everything possible to steal a road victory against an AFC powerhouse. They intercepted Allen inside the twenty-yard line twice via Alohi Gilman and Nohl Williams. That kept the scoreboard within reach. Running back Emmett Johnson carried a heavy load with 72 rushing yards and a second-quarter touchdown. Travis Kelce hauled in four passes for 71 yards to eclipse 1,300 career receptions. However, Kansas City’s offense sputtered repeatedly. They managed just 241 total yards and endured five three-and-outs. Harrison Butker pushed a potential go-ahead 46-yard field goal wide right with six minutes remaining. Another late three-and-out and a partially tipped Matt Araiza punt set up Bass’s decisive boot as time expired. Special teams Kansas City’s special teams unit usually serves as a reliable stabilizer in tight contests. However, it turned into an absolute liability when Kansas City needed precision most. The most glaring failure belonged to Butker. His wide-right miss from 46 yards out with six minutes left left critical points off the board. Sure, Butker remained automatic inside 39 yards. That said, his miss dropped him to a dismal eight-of-sixteen on attempts from 40 yards or longer this season. That’s a glaring contrast to Bass drilling kicks from 54 and 57 yards on the exact same soggy turf. To make matters worse, punter Matt Araiza endured a nightmarish evening. It was capped by a partially tipped punt in the final fifteen seconds. That allowed Greg Dortch to return the ball seventeen yards to Kansas City’s 39-yard line. It handed Buffalo effortless winning field position. item.title: SCU Torreense 1-2 Celtic – It’s not ’embarrassing’, it’s a valuable victory
item.description: SCU Torreense 1-2 Celtic – It’s not ’embarrassing’, it’s a valuable victory A win is a win. It’s certainly not embarrassing as some have suggested. So stop the whining, it’s time to take a reality check… Players of Celtic celebrate after Javi Vazquez of SC Uniao Torreense scored an own goal to make it the first goal for Celtic during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Celtic massively boosted our chances of qualification from the Europa League group stage by recording a hard fought 2-1 win in Portugal over SCU Torreense to move up to 25th place in the Europa League group standings. It was a fixture seen by many as a potential banana skin, due to our history of away clashes in European competition, but the players dug deep and showed their determination to grind out a win on a difficult playing surface. It’s the kind of result that could prove ever vital in the long run as Martin O’Neill’s side look forward to the next away day challenge in Cyprus next month. Kasper Hogh of Celtic receives medical attention during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Right now I’d bite your hands off for a repeat of last night’s result, even with a similar performance. However, it doesn’t seem to be enough for a section of our supporters who have still found time to be critical of the manager and players in-spite of a win on the road in European competition. The headline I saw this morning was about how Celtic’s embarrassing run in Europe continues and had I not know the score then I would have thought reading that nonsense that we had lost to the Portuguese second tier side. Fans of Celtic show their support in the stands during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates with teammates after scoring his team’s second goal during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Celtic FC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on November 26, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) An early own goal, then a headed goal from Camilo Duran from a wonderful James Forrest cross gave Celtic a second successive victory in the Europa League, just weeks after the 3-2 win over Besiktas at Celtic Park.
