item.title: Liverpool plot ambitious summer window with Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala and Monza sensation Gustavo Varela on radar
item.description: FC Bayern München v 1. FC Köln - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool are reportedly plotting an ambitious summer transfer window with Bayern Munich midfielder Jamal Musiala and Monza striker Gustavo Varela firmly on their radar. While the Reds are prepared to explore a costly move for the Germany international if he proves his fitness, they are also well-placed to pursue Serie A's breakout forward. Liverpool eye ambitious summer deals According to Football Insider , Liverpool are ready to explore a summer deal for Musiala alongside their interest in Monza sensation Varela . Reports in Germany suggest the 23-year-old Bayern midfielder has a release clause active next summer, putting long-term admirers on alert. However, sources warn it would be a "very expensive" move, meaning the Reds first need him to prove his fitness. Bayern worried about Musiala's future Musiala has endured a difficult campaign after developing a neurological condition that has occasionally caused seizures during matches. Despite featuring heavily for Germany at the World Cup in the summer, he has managed just one Bundesliga start so far this term as Bayern work to help him get to the bottom of the issue. The report states that the Bundesliga giants are "worried" about Musiala's future and remain sceptical over whether he can return to his best. Occupying a "huge contract" in Munich, the club are concerned about paying lofty wages to a player who is rarely available, sparking a controversial debate in German football that Liverpool are monitoring closely. Monza striker catches Reds' attention Alongside their pursuit of Musiala, Liverpool have also received encouragement in their hunt for attacking reinforcements in Italy. The outlet revealed that the Premier League side are well-placed to "tempt" 21-year-old Monza striker Varela into a switch to Anfield next summer. Varela has emerged as a surprise package in Serie A during the 2026-27 campaign, netting an impressive 11 goals in his opening 11 league appearances. With Liverpool already tracking his rapid progress closely, sources indicate that Monza are likely to entertain a sale at the end of the season, though the Italian club will not let their star man leave cheaply. Fitness and form will decide The coming months will prove decisive for both targets as Liverpool shape their summer recruitment plans. Bayern believe that ongoing health problems for Musiala would deter top clubs, leaving the Reds waiting for clear signs of improvement before committing to a bid. Meanwhile, Monza are prepared to drive up Varela's valuation if his prolific scoring run in Serie A continues.

item.title: €50m Uruguay Star Wants Manchester United Move
item.description: €50m Uruguay Star Wants Manchester United Move Manchester United Tracking Maxi Araújo as January Left-Back Question Grows Manchester United have spent months tracking Maxi Araújo, and according to Sport Witness , their interest remains active after seeing him first-hand in the 2-2 draw with Sporting. The key detail is simple enough. The player wants the move, United like the player, and the only real obstacle looks like the fee. Sport Witness report that a source close to the situation says the Uruguay international is “very open to joining the Premier League side”. That matters. In transfer talks, willingness from the player often does a lot of the heavy lifting. It does not close a deal, but it changes the temperature. Maxi Araújo Interest Looks Genuine This is not one of those stories built on one scout in the stands and a lot of noise. United have “closely followed Maxi Araújo for months”, and they used the Lisbon trip to take another proper look. Sport Witness add there is “mutual appreciation”, which usually means the groundwork has already been done quietly. Araújo also gave them something tangible on the pitch. He played the full 90 minutes against United and assisted Luis Suárez for Sporting’s opener in the 33rd minute. Over the season, he has made 15 appearances and was making his 14th start. Availability matters, and so does output. Photo IMAGO January Transfer Fee Remains Central Issue The numbers are clear. Araújo signed a new Sporting deal until 2030 in August, and that contract includes an €80m release clause. He is also on what Sport Witness describe as a “top salary at Sporting”. So nobody should expect a bargain. That said, the report adds that “€50-60m should be enough to take the player in January”. In modern terms, that is the real valuation point, not the clause. The problem for United is straightforward. The same source believes they are “unlikely to invest that amount of money on a fullback in January”. That sounds believable. Manchester United Left-Back Need Is Obvious United’s need at left-back is hardly a secret. Luke Shaw has again missed time with injury, while Harry Amass remains more of a developing option than a guaranteed solution. In Shaw’s absence, United have patched the role with Diogo Dalot and Lisandro Martínez. It works in spells, but it is still patchwork. That is why the final line in the report stands out most: “What is certain is that Maxi Araújo’s camp are open to Manchester United.” The player is interested, United are convinced enough to keep watching, and the position needs addressing. The only question is whether the club view Araújo as a necessity now, or a luxury they can delay until summer. Our View This is the sort of report that makes sense straight away. The left-back situation has dragged on too long and it keeps forcing compromises elsewhere. item.title: Liverpool star expected to leave the club in 2027
item.description: Liverpool star expected to leave the club in 2027 Federico Chiesa Transfer Latest as Liverpool Weigh January Decision Federico Chiesa’s Liverpool future is moving back into focus ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh reporting from Daily Mail suggesting an exit is again a realistic possibility. The Italy international has found minutes difficult to come by and that has shaped the conversation around his next step. Chiesa is now 29 and, after an encouraging reputation built in Serie A, his time at Anfield has yet to develop into anything close to a settled role. Injuries have disrupted him, selection opportunities have been limited, and life under Andoni Iraola has so far offered little sign of a breakthrough. His omission from Liverpool’s Champions League league-phase squad felt particularly significant. Decisions like that tend to sharpen thinking for all parties, especially when a player is already operating on the fringes and trying to rebuild momentum. This season he has made only one appearance in all competitions, which underlines how far down the pecking order he currently is. Photo: IMAGO January Transfer Window Set to Shape Chiesa Future There is still a degree of caution around any prediction because Chiesa has been close to leaving before without a move being completed. Even so, the direction of travel appears fairly clear. Liverpool will need to assess whether a permanent sale, a loan, or simply keeping him until the summer offers the cleanest solution. Contractually, there is no immediate pressure. Chiesa is tied to Liverpool until June 2028, which gives the club control and should help protect value. That could influence the structure of any deal, particularly if interested clubs in Italy push for favourable loan terms rather than a full transfer. Serie A Return Looks Logical for Liverpool Forward A return to Serie A feels the most natural outcome if movement comes. Regular football in familiar surroundings may appeal to the player, and Italian clubs would likely view him as a market opportunity if the financial package can be made workable. There is also mention of a lower-half Premier League loan or interest from Saudi Arabia, both of which would present very different sporting and financial calculations. For now, Liverpool’s stance will be key. Chiesa has made 51 appearances and scored five goals since arriving in 2024, but January may offer the clearest chance yet to reset a situation that has never fully taken off. Our View It feels like one of those transfers that made sense on paper but never really found rhythm. Chiesa has obvious talent, and there have been moments when it looked like he might still carve out something useful at Liverpool, but everything around him has felt stop-start from the beginning. The biggest issue now is clarity. If Iraola does not see him as part of the core group, there is little value in dragging this on until the summer and hoping circumstances suddenly change. item.title: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win
item.description: Virgil van Dijk praises ‘outstanding’ Liverpool teammates after Club Brugge win Liverpool 3-0 Club Brugge: Van Dijk Praises Champions League Response Liverpool did what good sides are supposed to do after a bad European result. They went away from home, kept control, took their chances and left with a clean 3-0 win over Club Brugge in the Champions League. After the frustrating defeat to Fenerbahce, when Liverpool had led twice and still came away empty-handed, there was a need for a proper response. They got one in Belgium. Alexander Isak scored twice, Florian Wirtz added the third, and the game was effectively a demonstration of efficiency. Photo IMAGO Van Dijk Sees Right Reaction Virgil van Dijk started on the bench, which remains an unusual sight in any major Liverpool fixture, and came on for the final 15 minutes. Even without starting, his influence was obvious. He said: “I am in the game, encouraging and trying to do the type of things I usually do when I’m playing.” He added: “Off the pitch, in the warm-up, in the dressing room, I try to do all the same things but obviously you have a bit less influence.” That is the point with senior players. If they are switched on, they matter whether they play 90 minutes or 15. Alexander Isak And Florian Wirtz Deliver Club Brugge arrived in form and posed a tactical problem with aggressive man-marking all over the pitch. Liverpool handled it well. They moved the ball cleanly, punished openings and never let the game drift into chaos. Van Dijk summed it up plainly: “Overall it was a very good performance against a team who have been in form. They can be tricky to play against as they go with man-marking all over the pitch. “But our guys were so clinical, so good in the way we kept the ball. Defensively, we were solid as well. A great night.” Van Dijk reserved special praise for the younger players and the defence, saying: “The whole back line did so good, Trey [Nyoni] as well in front of them. The whole team were outstanding.” That is the real takeaway. Liverpool did not overcomplicate the evening. They corrected the mistakes of the Fenerbahce loss, stayed compact, stayed sharp and got the result they needed. As Van Dijk put it: “It was important to show a reaction away after what happened away to Fenerbahce. That was a disappointing night for us. But it’s about how you deal with what’s coming next and we’ve done that pretty well.”

item.title: FEATURE | We need to talk about Joane Gadou and Joey Veerman
item.description: FEATURE | We need to talk about Joane Gadou and Joey Veerman “His market value easily increased by ten million euros,” explained Kicker’s Patrick Kleinmann after Joane Gadou’s performance against Arsenal. Valued at €28m in Transfermarkt’s latest market value update, expect the Frenchman’s stock to rise once again after his showing at the Emirates Stadium, as Borussia Dortmund showcased their newfound winning mentality in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium. In games gone by, Dortmund would typically collapse after going behind early, but they equalised through Maximilian Beier, before Jobe Bellingham struck after Julian Ryerson’s parried effort, only for the Englishman to be judged marginally offside. Then, Dortmund’s steely defence weathered a late Arsenal storm to secure a share of the spoils. Playing on the right side of a back three, Gadou announced himself. Bild awarded Dortmund’s towering Frenchman a rating of 2, Ruhr Nachrichten a 1.5 – in Germany, they use a school grading scale, so the lower the number, the better. We, meanwhile, awarded him Man of the Match (7) after his stellar performance, as did FotMob (8.1). His toughest challenge in a Dortmund shirt, Gadou kept Christos Tzolis quiet, and assisted Beier for the equaliser with a superb Dayot Upamecano-esque run, which started in his own half. Gliding through Arsenal’s midfield, he then exhibited excellent composure to find Beier, who cut inside onto his left before placing the ball under Kepa. No player registered more than his 16 defensive contributions, while Dortmund’s towering defender (standing 6ft 5in), covered almost every blade of grass down BVB’s right-hand side – he also won 8 duels, and 6 tackles. Again, the most of any player on the pitch. Joane Gadou’s heatmap – via FotMob Another summer arrival, Joey Veerman, has also thrusted himself into the limelight. After a difficult start to life in Dortmund, the Dutchman is establishing himself in a midfield pivot alongside Felix Nmecha. In several actions at the Emirates Stadium, Veerman was the one player willing to take control of the game, and take risks. With a 90 percent pass completion (46/51), no Dortmund player played more passes into the final third (10), or line-breaking passes (14) than the 28-year-old, per FotMob. Oozing calmness on the ball, as Arsenal pressed, Veerman was the one player who relieved the pressure in difficult situations. Ruhr Nachrichten described his performance against Arsenal as the player “wanting to solve everything with his playing style,” while Bild lauded Dortmund’s No.28: “The Dutchman is increasingly becoming the midfield maestro and playmaker.” It’s hard to argue against that. Appointed as sporting director in March 2026, Ole Book, who is relatively unknown outside of German football, having previously being employed by Elversberg, is creating quite the team. Gadou was his first signing, and Veerman is proving to be a success story. Factor in Greek duo Konstantinos Karetsas and Gia

item.title: Five things to look out for on 2. Bundesliga Matchday 13
item.description: Five things to look out for on 2. Bundesliga Matchday 13 2. Bundesliga leaders Hertha entertain relegation-threatened Karlsruhe on matchday 13, while bottom-placed Holstein Kiel host promotion hopefuls Kaiserslautern. Out-of-form Heidenheim host second-placed Nürnberg Miroslav Klose's side suffered their second defeat of the season against Eintracht Braunschweig last week, but they will be confident ahead of their game in Heidenheim on Friday. Frank Schmidt’s men are seven points behind the playoff spot after a seven-game winless run. On Friday, the coaches who are at contrasting points of their careers will lock horns for the first time at Voith-Arena. Heidenheim are unbeaten in their last five home games against Der Club, including their 5-0 victory in 2023 with four of the goals coming from the current Gladbach captain Tim Kleindienst. Two Lower Saxony derbies The four Lower Saxony clubs in 2. Bundesliga will go head-to-head on matchday 13. A day after newly-promoted Osnabrück host Hannover, Eintracht Braunschweig will welcome Wolfsburg, who are playing in their first second-tier season after three decades. Both Hannover and Wolfsburg underperformed compared to pre-season expectations, while Braunschweig and Osnabrück are playing to avoid the drop. Despite playing away from home, Hannover and Wolfsburg are the overwhelming favorites for this week's Lower Saxony derbies. Hertha welcome travel-sick Karlsruhe 2. Bundesliga leaders Hertha won all five of their first Olympiastadion games this season. On the contrary, Karlsruhe will travel to the capital city on the back of only picking up a couple of points from five matches on the road. Stefan Leitl's men already extended their lead at the summit to a staggering ten points after a 4-0 victory in Cottbus last week. Karlsruhe drew goalless with Osnabrück as both teams have 12 points from as many games. Kiel host Kaiserslautern in Kniat's home debut Michel Kniat's Holstein Kiel debut ended in a heavy defeat in Wolfsburg after they conceded three second-half goals. The former Arminia Bielefeld coach will make his Holstein-Stadion debut when the cellar-dwellers host Kaiserslautern on Saturday. No result could lift the hosts out of automatic relegation spots for now, but three points could go a long way in shifting their form before it's too late. Kaiserslautern have the league's best defense, although they dropped to fifth place after their 2-2 home draw with Dynamo Dresden. The surprise inclusion Emmanuel Iyoha joined Joel Grodowski, Felix Klaus and Mohamed Ali Zoma last week with his goal lifting Magdeburg to third place. item.title: Jason Kelce Fed Up With Biased-Refs Narratives As Controversy Erupts Over Questionable Officiating in Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Loss to Bills
item.description: Oct 11, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; NFL network game analyst Jason Kelce is interviewed on the field before the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. © Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs vs. Buffalo Bills showdown was the perfect way to end Thanksgiving night, but the visitors at Highmark Stadium were left with a sour taste in their mouths as Patrick Mahomes’ crew fell to a 13-10 defeat. On a rainy night at Orchard Park, both offenses struggled to get going, but one instance in particular gave rise to yet another heated debate about refereeing consistency. Philadelphia Eagles legend Jason Kelce, however, saw the funny side of that officiating decision involving Rashee Rice. Jason Kelce Speaks His Mind as Refs Overturn Rashee Rice’s Catch With the score tied at 10-10 and less than two minutes remaining in regulation, Patrick Mahomes found Rice over the middle on third-and-10 from Kansas City’s 9-yard line. At first glance, Rice appeared to have hauled in a pretty impressive one-handed catch despite taking a heavy hit. That would have been an 11-yard completion, but officials from New York stepped in to reverse the call following a replay review, forcing Kansas City to punt. Kelce wasted little time going on X to weigh in on the turn of events, writing , “Well, at least we don’t have to hear all of Twitter [expletive] about the refs being homers for the Chiefs tonight.” While Kelce’s hope was that the Rice call would finally put the refs-always-favor-the-Chiefs narrative to bed, there’s still a lot of action over the next few weeks for that storyline to rear its head. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid was clearly not convinced by the rationale to overturn the catch. In his post-game press conference, Reid told reporters, “To me, that was not clear and obvious,” arguing that the replay evidence did not warrant overturning the original decision. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor NFL Vice President of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth subsequently explained that officials determined Rice had lost control of the football upon making contact with the ground. Kansas City had another opportunity to snatch victory but failed to capitalize. A partially blocked Matt Araiza punt eventually set up Bills kicker Tyler Bass for a game-winning 57-yard field goal as time expired. After the defeat, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany, made it a point to voice her complaints, going after the referees in an Instagram rant. “HAHAHAHAHAHA, WHAT A JOKE,” Brittany wrote on Instagram . “Guess we can’t even play football without getting it called against us. Not sure what an actual catch is after that, I guess? I don’t wanna hear [expletive] anymore from anyone.” Mahomes finished his night with a PFN QB Impact Grade of 71.8, while Allen graded out at 67.5. item.title: Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Singer-songwriter and record producer Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has said the “rig and die” slogan sounds correct as a response to election rigging, but warned that innocent people must not be caught up in the resulting violence. He spoke in an interview on Nigeria Info’s WhatsUpLagos show while responding to the slogan ahead of the 2027 elections. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzle money and die. Na death penalty for China for embezzlement.” He said Nigeria needed serious deterrence for crimes, including kidnapping, and that people were frustrated by what he described as a lack of consequences. “We’re in a stage where we need, we need serious deterrence, anybody who kidnaps is supposed to face serious consequences. “Because it’s getting too much, and people are just getting away with everything. You understand what I’m saying? So for me, the statement itself, it shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone by. So for me, I don’t see nothing wrong with that statement.” However, he warned against innocent people being harmed in the name of enforcing the slogan. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this fight because some people might not rig, they might just be there. It could be jungle justice without proving that the person actually rigged.” He said the burden of proof should rest on the accusers, while reiterating his support for the statement. “So that’s where, that’s where it becomes dangerous. So the burden of proof should be on the accused person, but the statement in itself, I am in full support of it.” The post Nothing wrong with ‘rig and die’, but innocent people must not be targeted — 2Baba appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nvidia: Women Raise Concerns Over Jensen Huang’s Return
item.description: News of Jensen Huang’s shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power — across politics and business. Meanwhile, many “tech bros” rushed to Huang’s defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a “hero” and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang’s resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. “They’re standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want,” Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be “hero worship,” she said. It also reflects the tech industry’s mythology around “founder mode” — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Another of Huanga’s alleged lovers was a subordinate at Nvidia. “This is a great example of why integrity matters,” Kunst said. “As soon as I heard about the honeypot element, it was clear to me that there were lapses in judgment that were really big.” On November 17, board Chairman Harvey Jones said the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Then President Donald Trump intervened. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC, referring to Huang’s reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions as punishment. item.title: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
item.description: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015 , both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric . As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market . At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets. So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base. Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. There’s also new, modern infotainment and interiors that are now even nicer to spend time in than before. Read full article Comments

item.title: I belong to APC but will protect all parties — Defence Minister
item.description: The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, has said his membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) does not prevent him from carrying out his responsibility to provide security for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. Musa, a retired general, said he was entitled to associate with the ruling party because he was no longer serving in the military. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Arise Television, where he was asked to explain his participation in APC political activities and how he intended to separate his party affiliation from his official duties. “Well, I’m not a military man. I belong to APC, I’m allowed to do that,” he said. The former Chief of Defence Staff maintained that his appearances at political events were also an opportunity to assess security arrangements and ensure that security agencies were performing their duties. He stressed, however, that the responsibility applied to all political parties. “I always want to make sure that whatever is happening anywhere, I go there to ensure that the security forces are doing what they should, and we can do that for everybody. It’s not just for APC. “We are free-minded, we are fair-minded to everybody. We want Nigeria to be safe. We’ll never be a party to any violence,” he said. The minister said President Bola Tinubu had repeatedly cautioned members of his administration against electoral violence. “I know the President has told us on several occasions when we meet, ‘I do not want a violent election. It is not worth it,’” he added. Musa also pledged that the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces would collaborate with political parties and other stakeholders to ensure credible elections in 2027. “Nigerians must understand that we must make our elections free and fair and credible. So we, members of the Armed Forces and the Defence, will ensure that we work together with everyone to make the elections free. “We want every Nigerian to be free to come out and vote for whoever he wants,” he said. On complaints by opposition parties about political violence, Musa argued that disagreements within political parties could also trigger clashes. “Within all the parties, yes! We have found sometimes you see them because somebody feels somebody shouldn’t be there or his name was replaced for whatever reason, then he wants to sabotage from within. So the enemy is not only outside, it’s also within. “Whether the opposition or the party in government, violence is a no-no. And Defence is standing on its feet to ensure that the coming election is free and fair. Whatever it takes for us to do that, we will do that,” he said. The minister urged Nigerians to reject attempts by politicians to recruit them for violent activities, warning that those who lost their lives in political clashes could not be brought back. “We believe that if people are sensitised quite well and they see the folly of going into what they are doing, I mean, look at the few ones that h

item.title: Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world. “I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.” Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls. His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making. “I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Trump said Thursday. “So I really… think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world,” Trump said of the effort to back Huang. Asked if he had spoken with Huang since his reinstatement was announced, Trump said no, but then later said: “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.” He also praised Huang’s wife as “phenomenal.” The post Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Support team put in an emergency order for vodka – lots of vodka – to bring PCs back online
item.description: The end of the working week is often enough to drive tech support people to drink, which is why The Register likes to get the party started early. Friday mornings bring a new installment of On Call – the column in which we share your stories of doing whatever it takes to keep tech running. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Bruce," who told us that in the mid-2000s he worked for a global radio station. "We used to have about 30 PCs, all running slightly different radio shows depending on the time zone where we broadcast," he explained. The PCs were old clunkers running Windows 95 long after Microsoft ended support for the OS. Management knew the machines needed replacing, but funding was probably another year away. "We had to coax them on till then," Bruce wrote. "And by coax, I mean we were buying RAM on eBay because nobody sold the 4MB sticks we needed anymore." Thanks to the tender ministrations of Bruce and his colleagues, the PCs kept humming and the radio stations stayed on the air. Until a lovely spring Tuesday, when Bruce and his crew enjoyed a bucolic cup of tea in the first real sunshine of the season and received a call informing them that one of the stations was down. One of Bruce's mates figured a cranky old PC probably just needed a reboot and headed off to fix it while the rest of the team enjoyed their tea. And then the phone rang again to report another outage, so Bruce and the entire crew went back to work, chatting about which switch or other shared device could have taken out two PCs. When they arrived in the office, the chap who had gone to reboot the first PC ran in and announced that the computer room had flooded. Bruce and his teammates ran into that room and found dirty brown water all over the floor, walls, ceiling, and the racks holding the ancient PCs. "Water was even spraying out of the front fans of the last two PCs that were still working," Bruce told The Register . "After a lot of shouting words unfit to print, we all got to work ripping them out, shutting down what we could that looked to be working, and started lining them up outside in the car park," Bruce wrote. "Some of us then got to work stripping them down into component parts, others washed them down with isopropanol." As the isopropanol supply dwindled, one of the team arranged an urgent delivery of vodka. "Luckily, it was a gloriously sunny day, so we quickly rinsed the PCs and left them to dry, strewn all over the car park," Bruce wrote. By this stage, he and the team were all filthy and exhausted. With the stations still offline, they had to rebuild the PCs and get them running again. "We only lost two sticks of RAM, one sound card, and a power supply," Bruce wrote. item.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
item.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. The “rig and die” slogan has featured prominently in political discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly among supporters of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. item.title: CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH) and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are set to explore how digital identity can drive financial inclusion, trust and economic growth at the 2026 CeBIH Annual Conference scheduled for December 1 and 2 in Lagos. The conference, themed “Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial services leaders and technology innovators to examine the role of identity infrastructure in Nigeria’s digital financial ecosystem. Speaking at a press conference on the theme of the conference, Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, said the future of financial services and the broader digital economy depended significantly on reliable, secure and accessible digital identity infrastructure. “A trusted digital identity ecosystem has implications far beyond registration and identification. It can help address some of the structural barriers to financial inclusion.’’ Gbolahan Oluwatobiloba, Lagos State Coordinator, NIMC, said identity was the foundation of economic development, security and trust. “Identity is the foundation of everything, not just the financial sector, the security sector or the identity ecosystem. When you remove identity, your security will be affected, because how do you secure people you don’t know?” he said. Vice Chairman of CeBIH and Chairman of the Conference Planning Committee, Abednigo Ugwueke, said participants would examine how trusted digital identity could improve customer onboarding, strengthen Know Your Customer processes, enhance identity verification, reduce fraud and expand access to financial services. The conference is expected to feature key government and industry personalities, including NIMC Director-General, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr. Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr. Vincent Olatunji; and Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. Kayode Olubiyi, Head of Digital Payments, UBA, representing the CeBIH Advisory Council, said customers increasingly prioritised security and trust in banking. The post CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UNICEF, NGE, Lagos govt to tackle child survival, education challenges
item.description: By Ch ioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Stakeholders, yesterday, called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The stakeholders include the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, Lagos State Government and Airtel Nigeria made the call at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium themed: ‘Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility’ in Lagos. Speaking at the event organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME, President of the NGE, Mr. Eze Anaba, said the responsibility of ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential rested on all stakeholders, not government alone. Anaba cited a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, describing the figure as alarming and calling for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to examine their contributions towards addressing the problem. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms. Lone Hvass, said: “Survival, education and learning are deeply interconnected. A child who is out of school is denied much more than education. He or she is denied opportunities for protection, participation and the possibility of realising their full potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Sanwo-Olu Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr. Claudiana Sanwo-Olu, said children were not merely beneficiaries of government policies but individuals with rights, aspirations, talents and opinions whose voices deserved to be heard in decisions affecting them. item.title: AWS adds virtual iPhones to its cloud
item.description: AWS now offers two new types of cloudy computers: emulated Androids and simulated iPhones. The cloudy colossus announced both virtual offerings on Wednesday. They’re part of its Device Farm service, which previously saw AWS offer developers the chance to test their software on actual iOS and Android devices that reside in the Amazonian cloud. AWS will now also host virtual devices running Android and iOS. AWS touts the virtual mobile devices as superior to physical devices. “With virtual devices, you can shift testing left to stages that need high speed and volume, such as pull requests, code merges, and smoke tests, and keep real devices for later stages that need high fidelity, such as regression and release testing,” the cloudy business unit argues in its launch announcement. AWS also says developers can get to work faster on a virtual iPhone or Pixel. “Virtual devices running the latest device and OS typically start in seconds, and others start in around a minute,” the outfit argues. That may sound appetizing, but Amazon’s menu of virtual devices is short and bland. When The Register logged on as an AWS user, the only emulated Android phone listed was a Google Pixel 10, running Android 15, 16, or 17. An emulated Pixel tablet running Android 17 is also on the menu. At the time of writing, we could find only a virtual iPhone 16, running iOS 18.6, 23.61, and 27.0. Analyst firm Counterpoint’s list of the world’s top 10 best-selling smartphones in Q2 of 2026 does not include a single Pixel device. The iPhone 16 occupies 10 th place. iPhone 17 models occupy the first, second, third, and seventh place on the list. AWS might excite more developers if it adds emulators for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Galaxy A07 4G, A17 5G, A17 4G, and Galaxy S26, as they occupy the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth places on Counterpoint’s list. Amazon’s choice of a Pixel tablet is also an oddity given analyst firm IDC doesn’t list Google among its top five tablet vendors . Amazon does offer physical Galaxy A17 devices and three versions of the iPhone 17. But Device Farm doesn’t offer any foldable devices, meaning developers struggling to wrap their heads around the iPhone Duo will need either ask Apple for a loaner or shell out $2,000 to acquire one. At least developers don’t have to change behavior to access the few virtual devices AWS offers, as existing Device Farm APIs and test frameworks will work on real or notional machines. ®

item.title: Shivelyuch Socked In
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Shivelyuch Socked In Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the same way that Shivelyuch (also called Shiveluch) frequently displays volcanic activity, it is also chronically obscured by clouds. When the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image on November 8, 2026, clouds encroached on the snowy mountain on Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula . But they hovered beneath the volcano’s 3,283-meter (10,771-foot) peak, leaving a clear opening over its caldera and northern upper slopes. The upper reaches of Shivelyuch feature a caldera 9 kilometers (5.6 miles) wide that is open to the south. A lava dome , formed by vents extruding viscous magma, appears as a dark area within it. Lava domes on Shivelyuch go through cycles of growth and collapse, with collapses sometimes setting off fast-moving avalanches of hot ash and rock called pyroclastic flows . In November 2026, effusive eruptions of lava and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months , according to reports from the Kamchatka Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT). And despite frequent cloudiness, satellites regularly detect thermal anomalies from the volcano. On the day of this image, KVERT reported that a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers (75 miles) to the east. That kind of activity is relatively tame for the mountain. Explosions from Shivelyuch periodically send ash several kilometers up into the atmosphere, where it can travel great distances and pose risks to aircraft . In July 2026, an ash plume rode the jet stream over the Bering Sea into Alaskan airspace, according to news reports , prompting the cancellation of multiple flights. item.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
item.description: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens. The platform is called the Digital Infrastructure for Governance (Impact and Transformation) – aka DIGIT – and is a modular suite that offers common services such as authentication and payment collection. Third party developers can also create DIGIT modules, and plenty have done so and now offer add-ons that handle tasks as diverse as managing birth and death certificates, revenue collection, and running water treatment plants. DIGIT is ubiquitous in India, where all state and union territory governments use the platform, as do over 20,000 local government entities. India also exports DIGIT under its policy of turning software created for its own needs into “digital public goods” (DPI) that it happily gives away to other nations. Nine nations have implemented DIGIT to some degree, among them Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Burundi, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka India’s population is 1.4 billion. Indonesia’s is 280 million and Nigeria is home to 240 million. DIGIT is therefore used by governments that serve over two billion people, some of whom are now at risk thanks to CVE-2026-136706 , a 9.3-rated SQL injection flaw present in DIGIT which allows “improper neutralization of user supplied input while constructing SQL queries and execution in the affected User and Access Control Service components.” “An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted input through the affected API endpoint to the targeted system,” according to CERT-IN . “Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized disclosure, modification or deletion of database information on the targeted system.” eGov India, which oversees work on DIGIT, has released source code for an update that fixes the problem. While local government users of DIGIT typically access it as SaaS, through large implementations run by national or state governments, over 1,000 deployments are live across various cities and other entities. Those orgs can therefore add patching DIGIT to their urgent to-do lists, along with fixing Java , PHP , vCenter and any other widely used technologies that suddenly need an urgent security update. ®

item.title: The token factory never sleeps
item.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. That means they need to think harder about maintenance windows, existing management tooling and predictable deployment. And they'll often be retrofitting halls whose racks rarely draw more than 30

item.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
item.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain. "Threat actors define scope and targets for ARTEX, which then uses AI agents to set verifiable goals, define tactical steps for each stage of the operation, use tools to attack targets, create graphs to track discovered systems and res

item.title: 7 Years Later, Hollywood’s Most Notorious Fantasy Flop Deserves Another Shot
item.description: I vividly remember learning the phrase “uncanny valley” in 2019. First came the trailer for Sonic the Hedgehog that April, with those alarmingly human teeth. Then came the first trailer for Tom Hooper’s Cats in July. Suddenly, there was a name for a feeling I’d had my whole life. The uncanny valley is that uneasy feeling you get when something looks or moves almost like a real person, but some small detail makes the whole thing feel wrong. That feeling is a lot more common these days, now that AI-generated videos are everywhere. But it was Cats that really brought the uncanny valley into the popular lexicon.

item.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
item.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. That said, here are some others that I have tested and recommend: The Garmin Fenix 8 is $749 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , which is a 25 percent discount off its original price. Its higher price comes down to having more features than the Forerunner 265S, so it’s really best for someone who does multiple outdoor sports and could make use of its handy LED flashlight. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. item.title: 'Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home' at 40: 'Trek' has never been as joyous or fun as in 'the one with the whales'
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. (Image credit: Paramount) "I wanted to make it accessible to people who don't go to 'Star Trek' movies," Nimoy said in "The Fifty-Year Mission" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Altman. "I wanted to make it a movie-movie. It starts out like a 'Star Trek' movie and then makes a left turn. It is intentionally very different." "The Voyage Home" effectively closes the trilogy that began four years earlier with "The Wrath of Khan". The story picks up three months after Spock's regenerated body is reunited with his katra (spirit), though nobody ever explains why Kirk and the rest of the crew are all still wearing exactly the same clothes. Following the self-destruction of Enterprise over the Genesis Planet, the gang are heading back to Earth to face the music for a lengthy rap sheet that includes grand theft starship and insubordination on an epic scale. But as they voyage home (geddit?) in a reconditioned Klingon Bird-of-Prey nicknamed the Bounty — complete with a cloaking device that wil

item.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
item.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. From L-R: Oluwatomi Otuyemi, Senior PR Account Manager, M.Inc PR; Tamunotonye Waka

item.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
item.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

item.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
item.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. Want to get a closer look at the planets of the solar system and the stars beyond? Then be sure to check out our roundups of the best telescopes and smart telescopes for observing the night sky. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your astrophotography with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
item.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
item.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. "We need to understand what is working, where things are falling short and, crucially, what needs to change," said DCMS Secretary Lisa Nandy. The watchdog won't have to wait long for its
